categories.summary: Brazilian individual taxpayer number (CPF), eleven digits with two check digits; it identifies one natural person.
Brazilian company taxpayer number (CNPJ), numeric or alphanumeric. It names a legal entity, so it never produces a sink finding and appears in the inventory only.
notes: A sole proprietor's CNPJ can identify a natural person together with other data; detected to avoid false positives and kept at the lowest weight.

categories.summary: Brazilian general registry identity card number (RG); formats differ by state and have no public checksum.
Portuguese tax identification number (NIF), nine digits with a mod 11 check digit.
notes: A NIF starting with 5 or 6 may belong to a legal entity or a public body; verify. Every checksum-valid NIF is treated as personal in v0.1.

categories.summary: Spanish national identity number (DNI): eight digits and a control letter computed mod 23.
Spanish foreigner identity number (NIE): X, Y or Z, seven digits and a control letter.
Italian tax code (codice fiscale), sixteen characters with a check letter; omocodia letters are accepted.
German tax identification number (Steuer-ID), eleven digits with a structural rule and an ISO 7064 check digit.
Dutch citizen service number (BSN), nine digits that pass the 11-proof.
French social security number (NIR), fifteen characters with a two-digit key; Corsican departments 2A and 2B are handled.
notes: The NIR is tied to social security and health insurance records, so it is flagged as health-linked.

categories.summary: Passport number; formats vary by country and have no common checksum.
Any other national identity or social security number (for example an SSN), recognised by the field name only.
International bank account number (IBAN), validated by country length and mod 97.
Payment card number (PAN) of 12 to 19 digits that passes the Luhn check.
Bank account or branch number, recognised by the field name only.
Salary, income or other remuneration of a person, recognised by the field name only.
E-mail address.
Telephone or mobile number.
Postal or residential address (street, number, city).
Postal code (CEP, ZIP, código postal); precise codes can single out a household.
Full name of a natural person.
Given name of a natural person.
Family name of a natural person.
Mother's name, common in Brazilian registrations and used as a security question.
Date of birth; with other signals it can indicate a minor.
notes: Also a children indicator: under the ECA (Lei 8.069/1990 art. 2) a child is under 12; GDPR art. 8 sets the consent age at 16 and lets member states lower it to 13. The tool never asserts minority.

categories.summary: Age in years; with other signals it can indicate a minor.
notes: Also a children indicator; see the note on demographic.birth-date.

categories.summary: Gender or sex recorded for a person.
Nationality or citizenship.
IPv4 or IPv6 address.
notes: Treated as personal because GDPR art. 4(1) names online identifiers in the definition of personal data.

categories.summary: Device identifier (advertising id, IMEI, push token).
notes: Treated as personal because GDPR art. 4(1) names online identifiers in the definition of personal data.

categories.summary: Cookie or session-tracking identifier.
notes: Treated as personal because GDPR art. 4(1) names online identifiers in the definition of personal data.

categories.summary: Latitude, longitude or other location data of a person.
notes: Location data is named in GDPR art. 4(1); it is not in the LGPD art. 5 II sensitive list.

categories.summary: Data concerning health: diagnosis, medication, allergy, test result, blood type, medical record.
Genetic data: DNA profile or genome-derived attributes.
Biometric data such as a fingerprint, face template or voice print.
notes: Sensitive under the LGPD whenever linked to a person; under GDPR art. 9(1) only when processed to uniquely identify a natural person, so the GDPR value here is personal. Verify the purpose.

categories.summary: Racial or ethnic origin.
Religious belief or affiliation.
Political opinion or party affiliation.
Trade union membership.
Data concerning sex life or sexual orientation.
Philosophical belief.
notes: GDPR art. 9(1) lists philosophical beliefs. LGPD art. 5 II lists only membership (filiação) in an organisation of religious, philosophical or political character, not the belief itself; a field recording such membership is sensitive under the LGPD: verify.

categories.summary: Criminal convictions, offences or records.
notes: Personal under both regimes. GDPR art. 10 regulates it separately from art. 9, and the LGPD does not list it in art. 5 II; the rules map it through the criminal group of rules.json.

categories.summary: Parent or legal guardian of a person; points to a record about a child.
notes: Indicator only: it never asserts that a data subject is a minor. ECA (Lei 8.069/1990 art. 2): a child is under 12; GDPR art. 8 sets 16, member states may lower it to 13.

categories.summary: School, class or enrolment data; points to a record about a child or teenager.
notes: Indicator only: it never asserts that a data subject is a minor.

categories.summary: School grade or year; points to a record about a child or teenager.
notes: Indicator only: it never asserts that a data subject is a minor.

categories.summary: Field that marks a person as a minor, a child or under age.
notes: Indicator only. ECA (Lei 8.069/1990 art. 2): a child is under 12 and an adolescent is 12 to 18; GDPR art. 8 sets 16, member states may lower it to 13.
